report.outcome: Analysis delivered: taskfold folds finished task spans (start call → finish result) only above 0.8 budget down to 0.6, outermost span first, into fixed-shape records. Children of an open parent do fold while it stays open and are absorbed into the parent record on finish. Decay is a two-level, pressure-only summary ladder (no time or position term, unlike triptych); nothing is evicted — only record text shrinks, spans stay recallable by fold code.
decisions: evidence from real TestHost runs in /tmp rather than new repo tests — analysis only, no code changed
open: cascaded-abandoned subtasks absent from a parent record's children list
grandchild outcomes flattened away when a middle task is absorbed

tasks.title: Compare decay/eviction with triptych and other conductors

report.outcome: Compared taskfold against triptych (positional thirds of the cap, sticky activation, band re-summarized at each 90% crossing), thermocline (attention-ordered L0–L4 fidelity ladder with an age-based safety net and a hard-delete floor), keel-lite (per-block recoverable rungs, hysteresis 0.85/0.65, no locks) and agedSummaryConductor. Taskfold is the only one whose unit is a semantic span, whose decay is token-pressure-only with no time or position term, and whose ladder only shortens its own summaries and never deletes or re-summarizes.
decisions: decay is pressure-triggered, not time-based — the ladder name 'age' means eviction order, not elapsed time
